Subject: Next steps: procurement gating & buying channel (PO vs card) — Acme Corp

Hi Ethan / Sofia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next actions so procurement has a single place to act from: 

- Summary of conversation: Acme wants to move Redwood into a pre-prod evaluation for the Recommendations team. Primary blockers: procurement channel (PO vs corporate card), legal review timeline, and whether to go via AWS Marketplace (contracting preferences).
- Items I promised to share: V1 SOW, procurement checklist, and a short note on purchasing alternatives. Attachments included below.

Proposed immediate next steps (can we agree on these?):
1) Procurement confirmation: Ethan — please confirm whether your default is a PO/Net-30 flow or if card payments are acceptable for a pilot. If there is a procurement mailbox recipient we should loop in (procurement@acme.example?) please let me know.
2) Legal intake: if your legal team needs a copy of the SOW or a data handling FAQ, tell us a contact and we’ll push docs and a short executive summary.
3) Marketplace read: if you prefer AWS Marketplace for billing, we can map the difference (pricing parity, contract timing) — this typically adds 1–2 weeks to setup.

Attachments: [attachment: Acme_Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: procurement_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

I’ll follow up mid-week if I haven’t heard back — appreciate any pointers on where this is likely to sit in your procurement queue.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.example | +1 (415) 555-0194
From: Ethan Ball <ethan.ball@acme.example>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.example>
Cc: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@acme.example>, procurement@acme.example
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement gating & buying channel (PO vs card) — Acme Corp

Kimberly —

Thanks for the recap and the SOW. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- Preferred: PO / net-30 is our default for vendor engagements above $10k. For a short pilot under $10k we can often use the corporate card; however, approvals still need a PO to be raised internally for budget tracking.
- Marketplace: Procurement leans toward Marketplace to centralize billing, but Legal has to approve any terms that differ from our standard PO flow. Marketplace will likely add an extra touchpoint (we'll need to route to our cloud procurement lead).

Who from Redwood should our procurement inbox expect to receive the formal PO and SOW? Also, if you have standard NHS/DP clauses or a one-page data protection addendum, that would speed legal review.

Sofia — I looped procurement@acme.example per your suggestion; can you advise next internal approver?

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Ball
Procurement Manager — Acme Corp
ethan.ball@acme.example

Subject: Fwd: Next steps: procurement gating & buying channel (PO vs card) — Acme Corp

Kim / Rishi — forwarding the thread. Quick internal operational note for tracking:

- If Acme requires a PO + net-30, sales should provide a billing contact and the finalized SOW so finance can accept a PO and issue an invoice. I recommend we ask for "PO routing instructions" (who signs, AP email, PO template) in the first reply so it doesn’t get stuck in legal back-and-forth.
- For Marketplace: our Marketplace enablement often needs a dedicated AM onboarding step; if Acme picks that route, add 1–2 weeks in our forecast.
- Legal artifacts: attach a one-page data processing summary (I drafted one previously) and request the Acme legal intake email. This typically reduces review time by ~3 business days.

Suggested message to send to procurement@acme.example (one-liner to get procurement moving):

"Hi — attaching the SOW and a short procurement checklist. Can you confirm whether you prefer a PO (net-30) or card payment for a pilot, and share the PO routing address / AP contact? If legal needs any data handling artifacts, please let us know and we’ll provide them immediately."

I’ve attached the checklist and SOW above. I can jump on a 15-minute call with their AP team if needed.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example

Hi Ethan / procurement team —

Quick check-in following up on the SOW and checklist I shared earlier this week. Two quick asks to unblock on our side: 

1) Can you confirm preferred billing channel (PO/net-30) or whether a card is acceptable for an initial pilot? If PO, please share the PO routing email and any template we should use.
2) Does Legal need the one-page data processing summary I mentioned? If so, I can send that directly to your legal intake address.

If helpful, I’m available for a brief 10–15 minute call today to walk AP / procurement through the SOW and where to place the PO. Otherwise, if you can reply with the PO routing info, we’ll prepare an invoice and next steps on our end.

Thanks for the nudge — we want to make this as frictionless as possible.

Best,
